title: From Outcomes to Steps: Reliable Success-Aware Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.27623v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning for long-horizon language agents requires identifying whether intermediate actions make eventual task success more or less likely when supervision is available only at trajectory level. The main difficulty is that a critic with aggregate return-prediction accuracy may still fail to resolve the local value differences needed to assign credit to actions, especially under sparse feedback and function approximation. Conventional critics estimate future return, but policy improvement also depends on knowing whether each intermediate decision makes task success more or less likely. We introduce SCALE, an actor-critic framework that augments conventional return estimation with explicit prediction of eventual task success. At each interaction prefix, the critic predicts a return value and a Success Value, defined as the probability that the task will eventually be completed from that prefix. translated_title: 从结果到步骤：面向长程语言代理的可靠成功感知评论家学习
translated_abstract: 针对长程语言代理的强化学习，需要在仅有轨迹级监督的条件下判断中间动作是否使最终任务成功的可能性增大或减小。其主要困难在于：一个在总体回报预测上足够准确的评论家，仍可能无法分辨为动作分配信用所需的局部价值差异，尤其是在稀疏反馈和函数逼近的情况下。传统评论家估计未来回报，但策略改进还依赖于知晓每个中间决策是否使任务成功更加可能或更不可能。我们提出了SCALE，这是一个actor-critic框架，它在传统回报估计的基础上，增加了对最终任务成功的显式预测。在每个交互前缀处，评论家预测一个回报值以及一个“成功价值”，后者被定义为从该前缀出发任务最终能够被完成的概率。SCALE将成功价值的变化转换为（原文此处截断）
tldr: SCALE框架通过让评论家在每个交互前缀同时预测回报值和任务成功概率（成功价值），解决了长程语言代理在稀疏反馈和轨迹级监督下中间动作信用分配的难题。
en_tdlr: SCALE is an actor-critic framework that augments conventional return estimation with an explicit Success Value—the predicted probability of eventual task completion at each interaction prefix—enabling reliable credit assignment for intermediate actions of long-horizon language agents under sparse feedback and trajectory-level supervision.
